verdicts.line: Maya, you're a hustler and the product works. But half your sales are rented from Amazon ads and there's no moat until that patent issues. It's a great small business, not a venture deal. I'm out.
verdicts.feedback: Ad dependence and pending IP make this a lifestyle-scale business today.

verdicts.line: I love Jess. I love the story. But this is a gadget, sister, not a brand people wear. I can't add enough here to earn my piece. I'm out.
verdicts.feedback: Strong customer persona, but no community or identity yet.

verdicts.line: The Coke on the desk? That's the whole pitch right there. I'm not a gadget girl, but I'll bet on a woman who closes on the ninth visit. I've got an offer.
verdicts.feedback: Founder grit is the asset. Retail chains respond to the demo.

verdicts.line: Two-ten to make, fifteen to sell. Those margins make me emotional, and I don't do emotional. Here's how this works.
verdicts.feedback: Excellent unit margin; valuation should follow profit, not hope.

verdicts.line: In ten seconds I knew. That flip test is a hero. Fifty thousand units in six weeks, patent pending, and a founder who tells me the truth. I want to make an offer.
verdicts.feedback: A demonstrable, retail-ready hero product; IP needs finishing.
